constraints: VERB-AWARE DEDUP (cold-critic finding, corrects the mission frame's first sketch): _rail_prefix()/_rail() run for ALL SIX RAIL_VERBS (claim, current, start, advance, attest, attach), and _rail_position()'s mid-flight branch is verb-blind -- it derives its {imperative} substitution purely from spine state, not from which verb triggered it. For 5 of those 6 verbs (claim/start/advance/attest/attach) the RAIL line is the ONLY place the next imperative appears in that call's output -- it is NOT a duplicate there and must keep the FULL imperative text unchanged. The 2x duplication issue #420 describes is real ONLY for the `current` verb, where render_human()'s own ACTIVE line already prints the same imperative. So: make _rail_position() (or its caller) verb-aware -- pass the triggering point/verb through so the mid-flight token substitutes a short, verb-appropriate pointer (e.g. 'the ACTIVE gate above') ONLY when point == 'current'; for every other railed verb, keep substituting the full imperative exactly as today. A pointer like 'the ACTIVE gate above' would be FALSE on start/advance/attest/claim/attach output, which never prints an ACTIVE line -- do not ship a pointer phrase that is only true for one of six callers.

The five RAIL_STRINGS dict VALUES stay 100% byte-unchanged (frozen, measurement precondition for #145) -- this fix only changes what value is substituted for the {imperative} token, and only for point=='current'.
state() must stay a PURE projection (INV-2 in docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md) -- reading anchors/constraints off the task dict adds no side effect and re-runs no check.

render_human()'s first line 'ACTIVE {id} [{status}] -- {imperative}' is byte-exact pinned by the GoldenOutputBriefing test class (tests/test_checklist_engine.py, class starts ~line 3738, e.g. test_pending_active_task_shows_open_preconditions_and_next_start ~3746) -- these call E.current(cl) directly (the pure function, before any CLI-boundary RAIL wrapping), so they are unaffected by the RAIL fix but MUST stay green through the anchors/constraints rendering change; extend them, do not break them. CORRECTION: render_human()'s own docstring cites 'tests/test_checklist_engine.py:818' for this pin -- verified live this run that citation is STALE (line 818 is an unrelated require_session call in a different test class); fix the docstring's citation to point at GoldenOutputBriefing if convenient while you're already editing that docstring, else log it as a triage candidate rather than spending a separate gate on it.

DoctrineRail.test_rail_mid_flight (tests/test_checklist_engine.py ~1825) calls E._rail('current', cl) directly and currently asserts the OLD (duplicating) substitution ('Next: do g2. Run it.') -- this is the test for the exact bug being fixed, so it is EXPECTED and REQUIRED to change as part of this fix, not a pin to preserve. Update it to assert the new pointer text for point=='current', and add a sibling assertion (e.g. E._rail('start', cl) or E._rail('advance', cl) with the same fixture) proving the OTHER railed verbs still get the full imperative unchanged -- that second assertion is what proves verb-awareness rather than a blanket dedup.

Shared-file fence with workstream D (#422): touch only the RENDERING path (state(), render_human(), _rail_position(), the dispatch()-boundary call into it, _RAIL_STRINGS token substitution). Do not touch _check_condition or any postcondition/invariant-evaluation code -- that is D's owned path this wave. If a genuine collision surfaces, stop and report it as a blocker rather than editing D's territory.

Vestigial-fields question is CLOSED for this run: corpus inventory (grep across skills/**/*.json and .agent-work/**/execute.json) found anchors and constraints genuinely populated on ~20+ real archived gates with real structured content. Build the renderer; do not delete the fields.

Goldens/tests are written FIRST against the pre-fix code (captured red), then the fix lands and the same tests go green -- this is the acceptance shape issue #420 specifies ('goldens written before the change so the diff asserts the intended delta').

The completeness property test enumerates the fields a Task may carry (per docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Task table plus anchors) and asserts every POPULATED one appears in current's rendered output for a fixture gate -- not just anchors/constraints by name, so a future forgotten field is caught by the same mechanism.
Do not touch the RAIL echo's assumed-behavior-neutral-for-compliance question -- that is C's tracer's job (DESIGN_SPEC.md workstream B, 'Behavior dependency, stated'), not this gate's.

Windows: run tests with 'python -m pytest ...', not 'py -m pytest ...' -- this worktree's 'py' resolves to an interpreter with no pytest installed; 'python' has pytest 9.0.2 and the full suite (1621 passed, 2 skipped, 550 subtests, ~473s) is green on this worktree's baseline before this change.

constraints: Verify goldens genuinely preceded the fix (git log / diff order or the implementer's own stated red-then-green evidence), not tests retrofitted to already-passing code.
Verify the frozen RAIL strings were not reworded -- diff _RAIL_STRINGS and confirm only the substituted token value changed, and only for the 'current' verb.

Verify verb-awareness directly: confirm a test exercises _rail() (or the CLI output) for at least one non-current railed verb (e.g. start or advance) mid-flight and shows the FULL imperative still present there -- a fix that dedups unconditionally for every verb is a regression, not the fix asked for.
Verify no touch to _check_condition or other invariant-check code (workstream D's owned path).
